title: Climate Change
standard_text: The difference between weather and climate; the greenhouse effect; heat transfer in the atmosphere and the oceans; the carbon cycle and carbon sinks; feedback loops such as albedo; and natural and human causes of climate change. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 9 and 10: Science (2008), Science, Grade 10, Academic (SNC2D), Strand D: Climate Change)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Science (SNC2D) worksheets on climate change: weather and climate, the greenhouse effect, heat transfer by the atmosphere and oceans, carbon sinks, albedo and feedback loops. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Climate is the average weather over about 30 years.
key_sub: Greenhouse gases absorb infrared energy given off by Earth.
body_html:
How to think about it

Weather is what happens day to day; climate is the long-term pattern. Earth's climate depends on the balance between energy coming in from the Sun and infrared energy going out. Greenhouse gases absorb some outgoing infrared energy and send part of it back, keeping Earth warm.

The atmosphere and oceans move heat from the equator towards the poles by winds and ocean currents. Carbon moves between the air, oceans, rocks and living things; forests and oceans are carbon sinks. Feedback loops change the size of warming: melting snow and ice lower the albedo, so more sunlight is absorbed (a positive feedback).

Example

Fresh snow reflects about 80% of sunlight; open water about 6%. What happens when sea ice melts?

More sunlight is absorbed.

Answer: warming speeds up (positive feedback)

Example

Is 'it rained today in Toronto' weather or climate?

One day, one place

Answer: weather

Common mistakes

  • Confusing weather and climate.
  • Saying the ozone hole causes global warming.
  • Thinking all feedback loops make warming worse: negative feedbacks reduce it.

faq.a: The fraction of sunlight a surface reflects. Snow has a high albedo; dark forests and oceans have a low albedo.

faq.q: Why does the ocean affect climate?
faq.a: Water stores huge amounts of heat and currents carry it around the planet, which keeps coastal climates milder.

items.q: Emma is collecting evidence that Earth's climate is warming. Which is the strongest scientific evidence?
c: Mountain glaciers around the world are shrinking.
One summer day was very hot.
My friend says winters used to be colder.
A movie showed a big storm.
items.e: Strong evidence comes from many measurements over many years, not one day or one opinion.

items.e: Warm air at the equator rises, because it is less dense.

items.q: A light bulb warms your hand held a few centimetres beside it. Which process transfers the thermal energy mainly?
items.e: Conduction: through solids by particle collisions. Convection: in fluids by moving hot fluid. Radiation: by infrared waves, no medium needed.
